The investigated samples were GaN thin layers with embedded ferromagnetic γ'-Ga_y Fe_4-y N nanocrystals, fabricated by metal organic vapor phase epitaxy.
The nanocrystals had a face-centered cubic (fcc) structure with the (100) planes parallel to the [0001] c-growth direction of the wurtzite GaN matrix.
The size of the nanocrystals ranged from (50±20)nm to (20±8)nm in the layer plane and (17±8)nm along the c-growth direction.
The density of the nanocrystals was tunable by the amount of Ga provided during growth, ranging from 3.9 x 10^9 NC/cm^2 to 15.0 x 10^9 NC/cm^2.
The lattice parameter of the nanocrystals along the c-growth direction ranged from 3.789 Å to 3.806 Å, depending on the Ga content.
The Curie temperature of the nanocrystals ranged from 450 K to 500 K, decreasing with increasing Ga content.
The DAFS analysis confirmed the incorporation of Ga into the nanocrystals, with a maximum Ga occupancy of around 30% in the 3c sites of the fcc structure.
In contrast to previous reports on Ga_y Fe_4-y N powders where Ga occupied the 1a sites, the Ga atoms in the nanocrystals embedded in the GaN matrix preferentially occupied the 3c sites.

The saturation magnetization and Curie temperature of the nanocrystals decreased with increasing Ga content, indicating that the inclusion of Ga in the 3c sites does not significantly affect the magnetic properties up to 30% Ga.
The combination of AXD and DAFS techniques allowed the researchers to overcome the challenge of distinguishing between Ga atoms in the host matrix and those in the embedded nanocrystals.
The DAFS analysis showed that the Ga atoms in the nanocrystals occupied the 3c Wyckoff sites in the fcc structure, rather than the 1a sites.
The lattice parameter of the nanocrystals along the c-growth direction was smaller than the values reported for Ga_y Fe_4-y N powders where Ga occupied the 1a sites.

The researchers attributed the preferential occupation of the 3c sites by Ga atoms in the nanocrystals to the arrangement of the surrounding GaN matrix, where Ga tends to occupy lattice sites with N as nearest neighbors.
The DAFS technique allowed the researchers to quantify the amount of Ga incorporated into the nanocrystals, which ranged from 10% to 31% of the 3c sites.
The magnetic properties of the nanocrystals, including the saturation magnetization and Curie temperature, were inversely correlated with the amount of Ga incorporated into the 3c sites.
